title: Bounded etale dualizing objects and their coefficient counit mates
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $1\le m\le n$. Set $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^m)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], write $a_Y:Y\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $F_{Y,R}=Ra_{Y,R!}\dashv G_{Y,R}=a_{Y,R}^{\times}$, $\omega_{Y,R}=G_{Y,R}R_s$, and $\varepsilon_{Y,R}:F_{Y,R}\omega_{Y,R}\to R_s$, for $R=A,B$, on ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $T_Y=-\otimes_A^LB$ [def-kun-derived-tensor], and denote the canonical compact-support coefficient comparison by $c_{Y,K}:T_sF_{Y,A}K\to F_{Y,B}T_YK$ [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Here bounded constructible finite-Tor means constructible cohomology, zero outside a finite interval, and integers $a\le b$ such that tensoring with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. For every such $Y$, the compactification-independent functors $F_{Y,R}$ and their ordinary etale right adjoints exist, $Y$ is Noetherian, and $\omega_{Y,R}$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},R)$. Whenever $\omega_{Y,A}$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, define $u_Y:T_Y\omega_{Y,A}\to\omega_{Y,B}$ to be the unique map with $\varepsilon_{Y,B}F_{Y,B}(u_Y)=(T_s\varepsilon_{Y,A})c_{Y,\omega_{Y,A}}^{-1}$, using $T_sA_s\cong B_s$. The same assertions hold at every further positive quotient level $C=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi^h)$, $h\le m$. There is the following normalization for their use in a factorization $Y\xrightarrow i P\xrightarrow p s$: whenever $Q$ and $Q'$ are bounded-below objects representing the same functor $L\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(F_{pi}L,N)$ on $D^+$, the comparison induced by those Hom bijections is the unique counit-compatible isomorphism. Under $F_pF_i\cong F_{pi}$ its counit is $\varepsilon_{pi}=\varepsilon_pF_p(\varepsilon_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. On bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs the canonical coefficient comparisons obey $c_{pi,K}=F_{p,B}(c_{i,K})c_{p,F_{i,A}K}$ with the compact-support composition identifications [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons, lem-sf-compact-coefficient-composition].

proof.text: For the finite quotient homomorphism, apply the already proved compactSupport_isIso helper in ExceptionalCoefficientComparison: properFiniteCoefficientExtension is invertible on every input, and the open scalar comparison is an isomorphism. This is the ordinary-etale compact-scalar coherence argument [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence]. Unfold the normalized dualizingScalarMap into mateMap followed by the right adjoint of unitIso. Naturality of the B-counit moves this unit map after the counit; the inverse adjunction Hom bijection evaluated at mateMap then gives comparisonInverse followed by scalar extension of the A-counit and unitIso. Finally injectivity of the inverse Hom bijection proves that a map obeys this counit equation if and only if it equals dualizingScalarMap [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection, def-per-exceptional-coefficient-maps].

source.place: Paragraph 1: the compact-support coefficient comparison constructs the displayed adjoint map

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ and $H(L)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_{pi}L,N)$. For the two representing objects, write $\phi_L:\operatorname{Hom}(L,Q)\cong H(L)$ and $\phi'_L:\operatorname{Hom}(L,Q')\cong H(L)$ for the given natural bijections. The natural isomorphism $\beta_L=(\phi'_L)^{-1}\phi_L$ is represented by a unique map $\theta:Q\to Q'$ by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. Explicitly $\theta=\beta_Q(1_Q)$ and naturality gives $\beta_L(f)=\theta f$. The inverse natural isomorphism gives $\theta':Q'\to Q$; faithfulness gives $\theta'\theta=1_Q$ and $\theta\theta'=1_{Q'}$. Write $e=\phi_Q(1_Q)$ and $e'=\phi'_{Q'}(1_{Q'})$ for the universal counit maps. Naturality now says $e'F_{pi}(\theta)=e$. Conversely a map $t$ satisfying this equation has $\phi'_Q(t)=e=\phi_Q(1_Q)$, hence $t=\theta$ by injectivity. This proves the claimed unique counit-compatible isomorphism wholly inside $D^+$; the bounded-below hypotheses ensure that $Q$ and $Q'$ themselves are allowable test objects.

source.place: Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda), applied to the full bounded-below derived category and the given representing bijections

proof.text:
For a factorization in the statement, use the compact-support composition identification $F_pF_i\cong F_{pi}$ and compose the two adjunction Hom bijections. By [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], their composite has right adjoint $G_iG_p$ and counit at $N$
$$F_pF_iG_iG_pN\xrightarrow{F_p(\varepsilon_{i,G_pN})}F_pG_pN\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{p,N}}N.$$
Thus whenever this composite and another bounded-below object represent the stipulated functor on $D^+$, step 6 identifies them by exactly the unique comparison preserving this counit. After the specified composition identifications, the formula is $\varepsilon_{pi}=\varepsilon_p\circ F_p(\varepsilon_i)$. This is a normalization conditional on the representing objects in the statement, and requires no claim that an arbitrary unbounded right adjoint preserves $D^+$.

source.place: Tag 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits), with the two Hom bijections composed and step 6 applied

proof.text: For the factorization i then p, obtain Noetherian source and middle scheme from their finite-type structure maps [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Finite Tor amplitude makes the scalar extension of K bounded below: tensor with the coefficient sheaf B and use scalarTensorIso and exact faithful scalar restriction to detect homology vanishing, as proved in scalarExtension_plus_of_finiteTor [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Apply the exact existing etaleCompactScalarComposition theorem [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence]. Its compactScalarChosenMap component is definitionally ExceptionalCoefficients.compactSupportMap at the chosen compactification, so this is exactly the required equality with unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso. No conversion to arbitrary CoefficientTensorModel presentations or extra compatibility statement is required.
